english.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken equivalent when “actually” corrects or contrasts a claim.

exampleSentences.english: Actually, I don't like spicy food.
exampleSentences.jyutping: kei4 sat6 ngo5 m4 zung1 ji3 sik6 laat6

english.note: Use this specifically to introduce an actual fact or correction, rather than to add emotional emphasis.

exampleSentences.english: Actually, I really don't know him.
exampleSentences.jyutping: kei4 sat6 ngo5 m4 sik1 keoi5

english.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice when indeed means “actually” or “in fact.”

exampleSentences.english: Indeed, I haven't seen this movie.
exampleSentences.jyutping: kei4 sat6 ngo5 mei6 tai2 gwo3 ni1 tou3 hei3

english.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for saying that something is essentially or in effect the case.

exampleSentences.english: I’m effectively unavailable today, so I’ll go tomorrow.
exampleSentences.traditional: 其實我今日唔得閒，聽日先去啦。
exampleSentences.jyutping: kei4 sat6 ngo5 gam1 jat6 m4 dak1 haan4 ting1 jat6 sin1 heoi3 laa1
